questions.explanation: Arranging 8 distinct objects in a line is a permutation of all of them, giving 8 factorial which equals 40320.
questions.hint: Count every ordering of the distinct objects.

Wrong belief "chooses a committee of the wrong size" gives 36, not 84.
Wrong belief "forces one particular person onto the committee" gives 28, not 84.

questions.explanation: Since committee members have no order, the count is the binomial coefficient C(9,3), which equals 84.
questions.hint: No roles means order is irrelevant, so use a combination.

stimulus.body: From 5 people, how many ways are there to choose a committee of 4 and then select one of its members as chair?

questions.stem: From 5 people, how many ways are there to choose a committee of 4 and then select one of its members as chair?

options.misconception: Wrong belief "forgets to choose the chair" gives 5, not 20.
Wrong belief "orders all committee members, not just the chair" gives 120, not 20.
Wrong belief "chooses the chair from all people rather than the committee" gives 25, not 20.

questions.explanation: First choose the committee in C(5,4) ways, then choose one of its 4 members as chair, giving C(5,4) times 4 equals 20.
questions.hint: Choose the group, then pick a distinguished member from that group.
